proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer z. By definition,
E(n,t)=\lfloor nt\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kt\rfloor}{k}.
We compute E(n,x+z). Since nz is an integer, the floor-translation identity gives
\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor nx+nz\rfloor=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz.
Likewise, for each k=1,2,\dots,n, the number kz is an integer, so
\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor kx+kz\rfloor=\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz.
Substituting these into the definition of E(n,x+z) yields
E(n,x+z)=\bigl(\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz\bigr)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz}{k}.
Splitting the sum,
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{kz}{k}.
Since \frac{kz}{k}=z for every k, the last sum equals \sum_{k=1}^n z=nz. Therefore the added nz terms cancel, and we get
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}=E(n,x).
Hence E(n,x+z)=E(n,x) for every real x and every integer z.
solver_summary: Used the floor shift identity termwise on nx and kx, then observed the resulting integer shifts cancel exactly in the definition of E(n, x+z).
vetter_reason: The proof correctly establishes integer-translation invariance of each floor term and shows the added nz terms cancel in the sum, yielding E(n, x+z) = E(n, x) for all real x and integers z. This matches the lemma statement and the root semantic sketch with no substantive drift.
